citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3512. Confirmation of receipt of application and voted ballot (2023)
content:
The secretary, in coordination with county election boards, shall implement an electronic
   free-access system by which a covered voter may determine by telephone, e-mail or
   Internet website whether:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3514. Election notices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3514. Election notices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3514. Election notices (2023)
content:
(a) Preparation of notice.--At least 90 days before an election other than a special election and as soon as practicable
      before a special election, the county election board in each jurisdiction participating
      in the election shall prepare an election notice for that jurisdiction to be used
      in conjunction with a Federal write-in absentee ballot.  The election notice shall contain all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3510. Federal write-in absentee ballot
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3510. Federal write-in absentee ballot
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3510. Federal write-in absentee ballot (2023)
content:
A covered voter may use a Federal write-in absentee ballot to vote for all offices
   and ballot measures in an election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3511. Receipt of voted ballot
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3511. Receipt of voted ballot
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3511. Receipt of voted ballot (2023)
content:
(a) Delivery governs.--A valid military-overseas ballot cast under section 3509 (relating to timely casting
      of ballot) shall be counted if it is delivered by 5 p.m. on the seventh day following
      the election to the address that the appropriate county election board has specified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3518. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3518. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3518. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (2023)
content:
To the extent permitted by section 102 of the Electronic Signatures in Global and
   National Commerce Act (Public Law 106-229,15 U.S.C. § 7002), this chapter may modify or supersede provisions of that act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3519. Construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3519. Construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3519. Construction (2023)
content:
This chapter is intended to be read in concert with the Election Code.  Unless otherwise specifically provided in this chapter, if any provision of this
   chapter is inconsistent with a provision of the Election Code, the provisions of this
   chapter shall prevail.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IV. Voter Registration›Chapter 15. Changes in Records›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Correction of errors in cancellation or suspension
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IV. Voter Registration › Chapter 15. Changes in Records › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Correction of errors in cancellation or suspension
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Correction of errors in cancellation or suspension (2023)
content:
If the registration of a registered elector has been canceled or suspended through
   error, the registered elector may petition the commission for reinstatement of registration
   not later than the tenth day preceding an election.  After a hearing on the application, if error on the part of the commission is proved,
   the commission shall reinstate the registration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections›Part IX. Conduct of Elections›Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters›PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3516. Equitable relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 25 Pa.C.S.A. Elections › Part IX. Conduct of Elections › Chapter 35. Uniform Military and Overseas Voters › PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3516. Equitable relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 25 Pa.C.S.A. § 3516. Equitable relief (2023)
content:
A court may issue an injunction or grant equitable relief appropriate to ensure substantial
   compliance with or enforce this chapter on application by any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 204. Eminent domain for private business prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 204. Eminent domain for private business prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 204. Eminent domain for private business prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition.--Except as set forth in subsection (b), the exercise by any condemnor of the power
      of eminent domain to take private property in order to use it for private enterprise
      is prohibited.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 203. Applicability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 203. Applicability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 203. Applicability (2023)
content:
(a) Authority.--Except as set forth in subsection (b), the limitations and protections set forth in
      this chapter apply to the exercise of eminent domain by a condemnor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 205. Blight
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 205. Blight
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 205. Blight (2023)
content: (a) Scope.--This section applies notwithstanding the act of May 24, 1945 (P.L. 991, No. 385)1, known as the Urban Redevelopment Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Definitions

content:
Subject to additional definitions contained in subsequent provisions of this title
   which are applicable to specific provisions of this title, the following words and
   phrases when used in this title shall have the meanings given to them in this section
   unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

content: (a) Condemnation and passage of title.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 201. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 201. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 201. Short title of chapter (2023)
content: This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Property Rights Protection Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Notice to condemnee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Notice to condemnee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Notice to condemnee (2023)
content:
(a) Written notice.--Within 30 days after the filing of the declaration of taking, the condemnor shall
      give written notice of the filing to the condemnee, to any mortgagee of record and
      to any lienholder of record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 202. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 202. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 202. Definitions (2023)
content:

   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Application of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Application of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Application of title (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--This title provides a complete and exclusive procedure and law to govern all condemnations
      of property for public purposes and the assessment of damages.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Security required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Security required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Security required (2023)
content:
(a) Bond.--Except as provided in subsection (b), every condemnor shall give security to effect
      the condemnation by filing with the declaration of taking its bond, without surety,
      to the Commonwealth for the use of the owner of the property interests condemned,
      the condition of which shall be that the condemnor shall pay the damages determined
      by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 206. Extraterritorial takings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 206. Extraterritorial takings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 206. Extraterritorial takings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as set forth in subsection (b), no political subdivision shall exercise eminent
      domain authority against land that is situated in another political subdivision without
      the approval by resolution of the governing body of the political subdivision in which
      the land is situated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 207. Eminent domain of agricultural property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 207. Eminent domain of agricultural property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 207. Eminent domain of agricultural property (2023)
content:
(a) Approval required.--Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, approval by the Agricultural
      Lands Condemnation Approval Board shall be required prior to the exercise of eminent
      domain authority by any agency of the Commonwealth or political subdivision or municipal
      authority on agricultural property under section 204(b)(3) (relating to eminent domain
      for private business prohibited) or 205 (relating to blight).  Approval shall be obtained in accordance with section 13 of the act of June 30,
      1981 (P.L. 128, No. 43)1, known as the Agricultural Area Security Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 208. Eminent domain of land subject to conservation easement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. Limitations on Use of Eminent Domain › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 208. Eminent domain of land subject to conservation easement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 208. Eminent domain of land subject to conservation easement (2023)
content:
(a) Approval required.--Except as provided in subsection (g), no political subdivision, authority, public
      utility or other body having or exercising powers of eminent domain shall condemn
      any land subject to a conservation easement for any purpose, unless prior approval
      has been obtained from the orphans' court of the county in which the land is located.  The condemnation approval specified by this subsection shall not be required for
      an underground public utility facility that does not permanently impact the open space
      benefits protected by the conservation easement.  The condemnation approval specified by this subsection shall not be required for
      any public utility facility or other project that is subject to approval by a Federal
      agency, the necessity for the propriety and environmental effects of which has been
      reviewed and ratified or approved by the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission or
      the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, regardless of whether the right to establish
      and maintain such underground or other public utility facility is obtained by condemnation
      or by agreement with the owner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title

content: (a) Filing and exclusive method of challenging certain matters.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Recording notice of condemnation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Recording notice of condemnation (2023)
content: (a) County of recording.--

content: (a) Possession or right of entry of condemnor.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Revocation of condemnation proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Revocation of condemnation proceedings (2023)
content: (a) Declaration of relinquishment.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Venue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Venue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Venue (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A condemnation proceeding shall be brought in the court of the county in which the
      property is located or, if the property is located in two or more counties, in the
      court of any one of the counties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Agreement as to damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Agreement as to damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Agreement as to damages (2023)
content:
At any stage of the proceedings, the condemnor and the condemnee may agree upon all
   or any part or item of the damages and proceed to have those parts or items not agreed
   upon assessed as provided in this chapter.  The condemnor may make payment of any part or item agreed upon.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Additional condemnees, mortgagees and intervention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Additional condemnees, mortgagees and intervention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Additional condemnees, mortgagees and intervention (2023)
content:
(a) Identification.--The condemnee, at or before the hearing at which the claim is presented, shall furnish
      the viewers and the condemnor with the names and addresses of all other condemnees
      known to the condemnee to have an interest in his property and the nature of their
      interests and the names and addresses of all mortgagees and lienholders of record
      known to the condemnee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Right to enter property prior to condemnation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Right to enter property prior to condemnation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Right to enter property prior to condemnation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Prior to the filing of the declaration of taking, the condemnor or its employees or
      agents shall have the right to enter upon any land or improvement in order to make
      studies, surveys, tests, soundings and appraisals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Administrative matters for viewers' hearings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Administrative matters for viewers' hearings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Administrative matters for viewers' hearings (2023)
content:
(a) Facilities.--All viewers' hearings shall be held publicly in a suitable place within the county
      designated by the court.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 510. Powers of viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 510. Powers of viewers (2023)
content: (a) Proceedings.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Joint claims
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Joint claims
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Joint claims (2023)
content:
(a) Required.--The claims of all the owners of the condemned property, including joint tenants, tenants
      in common, life tenants, remaindermen, owners of easements or ground rents and all
      others having an interest in the property and the claims of all tenants, if any, of
      the property, shall be heard or tried together.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Appointment of viewers

content: (a) Court to appoint.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Petition for appointment of viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Petition for appointment of viewers (2023)
content:
(a) Contents of petition.--A condemnor, condemnee or displaced person may file a petition requesting the appointment
      of viewers, setting forth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Service of notice of view and hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Service of notice of view and hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Service of notice of view and hearing (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notice of the view and hearing shall be served, within or without this Commonwealth,
      by any competent adult in the same manner as a civil action or by registered mail,
      return receipt requested, to the last known address of the condemnee and condemnor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. Abandonment of project
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 3. Procedure to Condemn › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. Abandonment of project
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. Abandonment of project (2023)
content:
(a) Disposition of property.--If a condemnor has condemned a fee and then abandons the purpose for which the property
      has been condemned, the condemnor may dispose of it by sale, lease, gift, devise or

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. View
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. View

content: In every proceeding:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Furnishing of plans to viewers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Furnishing of plans to viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Furnishing of plans to viewers (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of condemnor.--The condemnor shall provide the viewers at or before the view with a plan showing
      the entire property involved, the improvements, the extent and nature of the condemnation
      and any other physical data, including grades, as may be necessary for the proper
      determination of just compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Appointment of trustee or guardian ad litem
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Appointment of trustee or guardian ad litem
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Appointment of trustee or guardian ad litem (2023)
content:
The court on its own motion may, or on petition of any party in interest shall, appoint
   a trustee ad litem or guardian ad litem, as may be appropriate, in accordance with
   general rules.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 513. Disagreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 513. Disagreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 513. Disagreement (2023)
content:
If a majority of the viewers do not agree on a decision, three new viewers shall be
   appointed by the court upon application of any interested party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 514. Filing of report of viewers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 514. Filing of report of viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 514. Filing of report of viewers (2023)
content:
(a) Time period for filing.--The viewers shall file their report within 30 days of their final hearing or within
      30 days from the filing of the transcription of the stenographic notes of testimony.  The transcription shall be filed within 30 days of the final hearing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Report of viewers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Report of viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Report of viewers (2023)
content:
The viewers shall file a report which shall include in brief and concise paragraph
   form:

content: (a) Extent of right.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 515. Reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 515. Reports (2023)
content:
(a) Multiple properties or claims.--The viewers may include in one report one or more properties or claims under section
      902 (relating to moving and related expenses of displaced persons) referred to them
      under the same or separate petitions if the properties are included in the same declaration
      of taking.

content: An appeal shall be disposed as follows:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 521. Liens and distribution of damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 521. Liens and distribution of damages (2023)
content: (a) Liens.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 520. Waiver of viewers' proceedings and termination by stipulation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 520. Waiver of viewers' proceedings and termination by stipulation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 520. Waiver of viewers' proceedings and termination by stipulation (2023)
content:
(a) Waiver of viewers' proceedings.--The condemnor and condemnee may, by written agreement filed with and approved by the
      court, waive proceedings before viewers and proceed directly to the court on agreed
      issues of law or fact.  The proceedings shall then be the same as on appeal from a report of viewers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Contiguous tracts and unity of use
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Contiguous tracts and unity of use
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Contiguous tracts and unity of use (2023)
content:
Where all or a part of several contiguous tracts in substantially identical ownership
   is condemned or a part of several noncontiguous tracts in substantially identical
   ownership which are used together for a unified purpose is condemned, damages shall
   be assessed as if the tracts were one parcel.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 522. Payment into court and distribution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 522. Payment into court and distribution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 522. Payment into court and distribution (2023)
content: (a) Payment into court.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Effect of imminence of condemnation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Effect of imminence of condemnation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Effect of imminence of condemnation (2023)
content:
Any change in the fair market value prior to the date of condemnation which the condemnor
   or condemnee establishes was substantially due to the general knowledge of the imminence
   of condemnation, other than that due to physical deterioration of the property within
   the reasonable control of the condemnee, shall be disregarded in determining fair
   market value.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Measure of damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Measure of damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Measure of damages (2023)
content:
(a) Just compensation.--Just compensation shall consist of the difference between the fair market value of
      the condemnee's entire property interest immediately before the condemnation and as
      unaffected by the condemnation and the fair market value of the property interest
      remaining immediately after the condemnation and as affected by the condemnation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Just compensation; other damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Just compensation; other damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Just compensation; other damages (2023)
content:
A condemnee shall be entitled to just compensation for the taking, injury or destruction
   of the condemnee's property, determined as set forth in this chapter.  Other damages shall also be paid or awarded as provided in this title.

content: (a) Contents.--The appeal shall set forth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Fair market value
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Fair market value
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Fair market value (2023)
content:
Fair market value shall be the price which would be agreed to by a willing and informed
   seller and buyer, taking into consideration but not limited to the following factors:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Removal of machinery, equipment or fixtures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Removal of machinery, equipment or fixtures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Removal of machinery, equipment or fixtures (2023)
content:
(a) Notice to condemnee.--In the event the condemnor does not require for its use machinery, equipment or fixtures
      forming part of the real estate, it shall so notify the condemnee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 519. Allocation of damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Procedure for Determining Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 519. Allocation of damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 519. Allocation of damages (2023)
content:
(a) Severance damages.--Upon appeal from an award of viewers, the court upon the request of the plaintiff
      shall, after the jury or the court, if the trial is without jury, has returned its
      general verdict, make a specific finding and allocation of the amount of the general
      verdict attributable to severance damages to the part of the property not taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Effect of condemnation use on after value
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Effect of condemnation use on after value
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Effect of condemnation use on after value (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In determining the fair market value of the remaining property after a partial taking,
      consideration shall be given to the use to which the property condemned is to be put
      and the damages or benefits specially affecting the remaining property due to its
      proximity to the improvement for which the property was taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Payment on account of increased mortgage costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Payment on account of increased mortgage costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Payment on account of increased mortgage costs (2023)
content:
(a) Reimbursement of owner.--Whenever the acquisition of property by an acquiring agency results in the termination
      of an installment purchase contract, mortgage or other evidence of debt on the acquired
      property, requiring the legal or equitable owner to enter into another installment
      purchase contract, mortgage or other evidence of debt on the property purchased for
      the same use as the acquired property, a legal or equitable owner who does not qualify
      for a payment under section 903(a)(2) (relating to replacement housing for homeowners)
      shall be compensated for any increased interest and other debt service costs which
      the owner is required to pay for financing the acquisition of the replacement property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Expenses incidental to transfer of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Expenses incidental to transfer of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Expenses incidental to transfer of title (2023)
content:
An acquiring agency shall, on the date of payment of the purchase price of amicably
   acquired real property or of payment or tender of estimated just compensation in a
   condemnation proceeding to acquire real property, whichever is earlier or as soon
   as is practicable, reimburse the owner for expenses necessarily incurred for:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Loss of rentals because of imminence of condemnation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Loss of rentals because of imminence of condemnation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Loss of rentals because of imminence of condemnation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A property owner shall be entitled to receive as special damages compensation for
      any loss suffered prior to the date of taking caused by a reduction of income from
      rentals which the property owner establishes was substantially due to the general
      knowledge of the imminence of condemnation, other than that due to physical deterioration
      of the property within the reasonable control of the property owner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Condemnee's costs where no declaration of taking filed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Condemnee's costs where no declaration of taking filed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Condemnee's costs where no declaration of taking filed (2023)
content:
Where proceedings are instituted by a condemnee under section 502(c) (relating to
   petition for appointment of viewers), a judgment awarding compensation to the condemnee
   for the taking of property shall include reimbursement of reasonable appraisal, attorney
   and engineering fees and other costs and expenses actually incurred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Consequential damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Consequential damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Consequential damages (2023)
content:
All condemnors, including the Commonwealth, shall be liable for damages to property
   abutting the area of an improvement resulting from change of grade of a road or highway,
   permanent interference with access or injury to surface support, whether or not any
   property is taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Limited reimbursement of appraisal, attorney and engineering fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Limited reimbursement of appraisal, attorney and engineering fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Limited reimbursement of appraisal, attorney and engineering fees (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The owner of any right, title or interest in real property acquired or injured by
      an acquiring agency, who is not eligible for reimbursement of fees under section 306(g)
      (relating to preliminary objections), 308(d) (relating to revocation of condemnation
      proceedings) or 709 (relating to condemnee's costs where no declaration of taking
      filed), shall be reimbursed in an amount not to exceed $4,000 per property, regardless
      of right, title or interest, as a payment toward reasonable expenses actually incurred
      for appraisal, attorney and engineering fees, except where the taking is for an easement
      related to underground piping for water or sewer infrastructure, in which case the
      reimbursement is limited to $1,000, regardless of right, title or interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Damages for vacation of roads
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Damages for vacation of roads
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Damages for vacation of roads (2023)
content:
Whenever a public road, street or highway is vacated, the affected owners may recover
   damages for any injuries sustained, even though no land is actually taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 716. Attempted avoidance of monetary just compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 716. Attempted avoidance of monetary just compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 716. Attempted avoidance of monetary just compensation (2023)
content:
Where a condemnor attempts to avoid the payment of monetary just compensation to which
   the condemnee otherwise would be entitled by use of a substitute for monetary compensation
   and the condemnee incurs expenses, including appraisal, attorney and engineering fees,
   in securing an adjudication that the substitute is not adequate, the condemnee shall
   be reimbursed by the condemnor for all these expenses incurred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Delay compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 7. Just Compensation and Measure of Damages › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Delay compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Delay compensation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Compensation for delay in payment shall be paid at an annual rate equal to the prime
      rate as listed in the first edition of the Wall Street Journal published in the year,
      plus 1%, not compounded, from:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Trial in court on appeal

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 11. Evidence›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Condemnor's evidence before viewers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Condemnor's evidence before viewers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Condemnor's evidence before viewers (2023)
content:
The condemnor shall, at the hearing before the viewers, present expert testimony of
   the amount of damages suffered by the condemnee.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Evidence generally
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Evidence generally (2023)
content: At the hearing before the viewers or at the trial in court on appeal:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Payments not to be considered as income or resources
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Payments not to be considered as income or resources
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Payments not to be considered as income or resources (2023)
content:
No payment received by a displaced person under this chapter shall be considered as
   income or resources for the purpose of determining the eligibility or extent of eligibility
   of any person for assistance under any State law or for the purposes of the State
   or local personal income or wage tax laws, corporation tax laws or other tax laws.  No payments under this chapter except those provided for in section 902(b) (relating
   to moving and related expenses of displaced persons) shall be subject to attachment
   or execution at law or in equity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Regulations

content: The General Counsel may promulgate regulations necessary to assure that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 11. Evidence›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Competency of condemnee as witness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Competency of condemnee as witness
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Competency of condemnee as witness (2023)
content:
The condemnee or an officer of a corporate condemnee, without further qualification,
   may testify as to just compensation without compliance with the provisions of section
   1103(2) (relating to trial in court on appeal).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Housing replacement authorization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 9. Special Damages for Displacement › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Housing replacement authorization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Housing replacement authorization (2023)
content:
(a) Short title of section.--This section shall be known and may be cited as the Housing Replacement Authorization
      Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 11. Evidence›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of condemned property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of condemned property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of condemned property (2023)
content:
In arriving at a valuation of the remaining part of the property in a partial condemnation,
   an expert witness may consider and testify to the use to which the condemned property
   is intended to be put by the condemnor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain›Chapter 11. Evidence›PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Viewers' hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 Pa.C.S.A. Eminent Domain › Chapter 11. Evidence › PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Viewers' hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Viewers' hearing (2023)
content:
The viewers may hear testimony, receive evidence and make independent investigation
   as they deem appropriate, without being bound by formal rules of evidence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish›PA ST 26 P.S. § 281. Entry upon land
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish › PA ST 26 P.S. § 281. Entry upon land
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 281. Entry upon land (2023)
content:
The Secretary of Forests and Waters,1the Executive Director of the Pennsylvania Game Commission or the Executive Director
   of the Pennsylvania Fish Commission,2on behalf of the Commonwealth, may respectively enter upon any of such lands, and
   take possession thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. General Provisions›PA ST 26 P.S. § 201. Fee simple title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. General Provisions › PA ST 26 P.S. § 201. Fee simple title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 201. Fee simple title (2023)
content:
When any political subdivision of this Commonwealth shall hereafter, in the exercise
   of the power of eminent domain, acquire by appropriation and condemnation any real
   estate, the title thereto which shall vest in such city, county, school district,
   or other political subdivision shall be a title in fee simple, unless prohibited in
   the ordinance or resolution authorizing the appropriation and condemnation thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish›PA ST 26 P.S. § 391. Control and supervision of lands acquired; income and revenue therefrom
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish › PA ST 26 P.S. § 391. Control and supervision of lands acquired; income and revenue therefrom
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 391. Control and supervision of lands acquired; income and revenue therefrom (2023)
content:
The Department of Forests and Waters,1or the Board of Game Commissioners, or the Board of Fish Commissioners,2respectively, shall have the control and supervision of all such lands acquired under
   the provisions of this act.  All income and revenue derived from said lands shall be expended in the same manner
   and for the same purposes as provided by law for the expenditure of the income from
   the State forests, State parks, or the receipts of said Board of Game Commissioners
   or Board of Fish Commissioners, respectively;  and, for such purposes, such income
   derived from lands acquired by the Board of Game Commissioners is hereby specifically
   appropriated, and shall be paid into the Game Fund;  and the income derived from lands
   acquired by the Department of Fisheries is hereby specifically appropriated, and shall
   be paid into the Fish Fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish›PA ST 26 P.S. § 261. Power of eminent domain
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish › PA ST 26 P.S. § 261. Power of eminent domain
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 261. Power of eminent domain (2023)
content:
Whenever the Department of Forests and Waters,1the Board of Game Commissioners, or the Board of Fish Commissioners2desires to acquire land, suitable and desirable for State forest purposes, for State
   park purposes, for game preserve purposes, or for the perpetuation or protection of
   fish, respectively, and a price for such lands cannot be agreed upon with the owner
   or owners thereof, or where such owner or owners cannot be found, in all such cases
   the Department of Forests and Waters, the Board of Game Commissioners, or the Board
   of Fish Commissioners is authorized to acquire the said respective classes of lands
   by condemnation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish›PA ST 26 P.S. § 361. Payment of damages awarded; costs of proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 5. Forests, Game and Fish › PA ST 26 P.S. § 361. Payment of damages awarded; costs of proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 361. Payment of damages awarded; costs of proceedings (2023)
content:
When the amount payable to the owner of such land has been finally determined, the
   same, adjusted in accordance with any amount previously paid into court as provided
   in section 2 of this act,1shall be paid by the Secretary of Forests and Waters,2the Executive Director of the Pennsylvania Game Commission or the Executive Director
   of the Pennsylvania Fish Commission,3as the case may be, from appropriations for such purposes or from the Game Fund or
   the Fish Fund.  All costs in connection with any such proceedings shall be paid by the Commonwealth
   in like manner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain›Chapter 2. General Provisions›PA ST 26 P.S. § 191. Land of historical interest to be exempt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 26 P.S. Eminent Domain › Chapter 2. General Provisions › PA ST 26 P.S. § 191. Land of historical interest to be exempt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 26 P.S. § 191. Land of historical interest to be exempt (2023)
content:
No corporation now incorporated under the laws of this state, or which shall hereafter
   be incorporated thereunder shall exercise the right of eminent domain as against the
   land now occupied by any building which was used during the colonial or revolutionary
   period as a place of assembly by the council of the colony of Pennsylvania, or by
   the supreme executive council of the commonwealth of Pennsylvania, or by the congress
   of the United States;  or as against the land now occupied by any fort, redoubt, or
   blockhouse erected during said colonial or revolutionary period;  or as against any
   building used as headquarters by the commander-in-chief of the continental army; 
   or as against the site of any such building, fort, redoubt, blockhouse or headquarters,
   which said building, fort, redoubt, blockhouse or headquarters, or site thereof, is
   now or shall hereafter be preserved for its historic memories and associations, and
   not for private profit:  Provided, That the said Colonial and Revolutionary period,
   as applied to the buildings, forts, redoubts, blockhouses or headquarters, or the
   sites thereof, as aforesaid, shall be taken as ended on the third day of September,
   Anno Domini one thousand seven hundred and eighty-three.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part III. Conservation and Natural Resources›Chapter 31. Water Resources Planning›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 3103. Intergovernmental cooperation and coordination

content:

content:

      information, objectives, priorities and recommendations to be considered and weighed
      in a broad range of State, local and private decisions.  The State water plan is not intended to constitute or contain legally binding regulations,
      prohibitions or prescriptions.

      information on the availability, distribution, quality and use of water resources

content:
(a) Interim registration program.--Pending the adoption of regulations for registration and reporting under subsection
      (b), each public water supply agency and each hydropower facility, irrespective of
      the amount of withdrawal, and each person whose total withdrawal or withdrawal use
      from one or more points of withdrawal within a watershed operated as a system either
      concurrently or sequentially exceeds an average rate of 10,000 gallons a day in a
      30-day period shall register with the department the source, location and amount of
      withdrawal or use or both.  Registrations shall be submitted not later than 12 months after the effective date
      of this chapter or 30 days following the initiation of any such withdrawal or use,
      whichever is later.  Registrations shall be submitted on forms as prescribed by the department.

content:

   to be an employee under the act of December 12, 1986 (P.L.  1559, No. 169),1known as the Whistleblower Law, in regard to good faith reports of potential violations
   of this chapter.  Environmental laboratories covered by this chapter shall be deemed to be an employer
   under the Whistleblower Law in regard to good faith reports of potential violations
   of this chapter.

content:

      upon approval of the Governor, to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

      and the act of June 23, 1982 (P.L. 597, No. 170),1known as the Wild Resource Conservation Act.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part V. Special Programs › Chapter 61. Environmental Stewardship and Watershed Protection › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6109. Sewage construction payments to municipalities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6109. Sewage construction payments to municipalities (2023)
content:
(a) Certain payments permitted.--A county or other municipality, municipal authority or school district receiving payments
      on the effective date of this chapter pursuant to the act of August 20, 1953 (P.L.
      1217, No.  339),1entitled “An act providing for payments by the Commonwealth to municipalities which
      have expended money to acquire and construct sewage treatment plants in accordance
      with the Clean Streams Program and the act, approved the twenty-second day of June,
      one thousand nine hundred thirty-seven (Pamphlet Laws 1987), and making an appropriation,”
      shall continue to receive all outstanding payments being funded under that act for
      the acquisition or construction of sewage treatment plants from the Commonwealth from
      funds appropriated for this purpose provided that the sewage treatment plant operations
      implement odor abatement programs as necessary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part V. Special Programs›Chapter 61. Environmental Stewardship and Watershed Protection›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6111. Protection of Recycling Fund

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6111. Protection of Recycling Fund (2023)
content:
(a) Market development funding.--The Department of Environmental Protection, on an annual basis, shall provide sufficient
      moneys for market development from the Recycling Fund to promote the long-term sustainability
      of recycling and to promote the continued growth of the recycling rate.  For purposes of this subsection, “market development” shall mean a set of government policies and programs that promote the removal of
      marketplace barriers to recycling and that promote a productive end use for recyclables
      collected from residents and businesses.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part V. Special Programs›Chapter 61. Environmental Stewardship and Watershed Protection›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Effect of repeal of site-specific postclosure fund provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part V. Special Programs › Chapter 61. Environmental Stewardship and Watershed Protection › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Effect of repeal of site-specific postclosure fund provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Effect of repeal of site-specific postclosure fund provisions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Prior to certification of final closure and release by the Department of Environmental
      Protection of the landfill bond under the act of July 7, 1980 (P.L. 380, No. 97),1known as the Solid Waste Management Act, and the regulations promulgated thereto,
      the trustee may release moneys from the trust to the county which established the
      trust upon written request from the county to the trustee in order for the county
      to spend the money to fund county conservation districts, protect farmland or accomplish
      any other purpose authorized by this chapter.  Payment of debt service by a county on obligations issued to fund such purposes
      shall be deemed to be paid for a permitted purpose.  Expenditure for farmland preservation must comply with the act of June 30, 1981
      (P.L. 128, No.  43),2known as the Agricultural Area Security Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part V. Special Programs›Chapter 62. Waste Transportation Safety›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6204. Waste Transportation Safety Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part V. Special Programs › Chapter 62. Waste Transportation Safety › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6204. Waste Transportation Safety Program

content:

      obtaining written authorization from the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part V. Special Programs›Chapter 62. Waste Transportation Safety›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6208. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part V. Special Programs › Chapter 62. Waste Transportation Safety › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6208. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6208. Penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Criminal penalties.--A transporter who violates the provisions of this chapter commits a misdemeanor of
      the third degree and, upon conviction for the first offense, shall pay a penalty of
      not less than $5,000 nor more than $10,000.  Upon the second or subsequent conviction of an offense under this chapter, a transporter
      commits a misdemeanor of the second degree and shall pay a penalty of not less than
      $10,000 nor more than $25,000, and the court may order the operating privilege of
      the transporter to be suspended for a period of up to one year, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources›Part V. Special Programs›Chapter 62. Waste Transportation Safety›PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6207. Enforcement

content:

      enforcing provisions of this chapter.  The authority granted under this section shall be exercised only when the employee
      is in uniform and is conducting an inspection of a vehicle as described in 75 Pa.C.S.
      Chs. 47 (relating to inspection of vehicles) and 49 (relating to size, weight and
      load).

content:
(a) General rule.--No municipal or residual waste processing or disposal facility shall accept municipal
      or residual waste from a waste transportation vehicle without a current authorization
      sticker issued by the department.  Failure to comply with this provision shall result in a penalty assessment of $2,000
      against the operator of the processing or disposal facility.

content:

   the money allocated annually to it under section 6104(d) (relating to fund) to provide

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part V. Special Programs › Chapter 63. Disposal Fee › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Disposal fee for municipal waste landfills
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Disposal fee for municipal waste landfills (2023)
content:
(a) Imposition.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), each operator of a municipal waste
      landfill shall pay, in the same manner prescribed in Chapter 7 of the act of July
      28, 1988 (P.L. 556, No. 101),1known as the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act, a disposal
      fee of $4 per ton for all solid waste disposed of at the municipal waste landfill.  The fee established in this section shall apply to process residue and nonprocessible
      waste from a resource recovery facility that is disposed of at the municipal waste
      landfill and is in addition to the fee established in section 7012of the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act.  The fee established by this subsection shall not be subject to the provisions of
      section 701(d) of the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 27 Pa.C.S.A. Environmental Resources › Part VI. Sanctions and Remedies › Subpart A. General Provisions › Chapter 77. Costs and Fees › PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 7708. Costs for mining proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 27 Pa.C.S.A. § 7708. Costs for mining proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Purpose.--This section establishes costs and fees available in proceedings involving coal mining
      activities.  The purpose of this section is to provide costs and fees to the same extent of section
      525(e) of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (Public Law 95-87,30 U.S. C. § 1201 et seq.) and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto.  It is hereby determined that it is in the public interest for the Commonwealth to
      maintain primary jurisdiction over the enforcement and administration of the Surface
      Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 and that the purpose of this section is
      to maintain primary jurisdiction over coal mining in this Commonwealth but in no event
      to authorize standards which are more stringent than Federal standards for the award
      of costs and fees.
